# Device Battery Status 1.2.0

Fresh percentage readings now support observational remaining-runtime estimates in the main popup and tray tooltips. Estimates need a meaningful timed discharge trend, adapt to sustained consumption changes and show rounded ranges. Categories, stale readings, charging and uncertain association never become invented runtimes. Runtime and capacity-based battery health remain independent.

Compact gaming alerts replace low-battery balloons. They show genuine percentages or native categories and honest runtime status, use non-activating click-through desktop windows, and coalesce repeated events. Settings provide global and per-device thresholds, optional confident-runtime triggers, monitor, duration, sound, snooze, cooldown and recovery. Sound defaults off. Preview uses synthetic data. Fullscreen/busy states can defer still-relevant alerts.

Includes the previously reviewed capacity-health infrastructure and background-efficiency improvements. Existing device tray modes, capacity history, diagnostics, installation, updates and deliberate manual polling-rate controls are retained. No additional hardware-query timer or background service is added.

Windows verification passed: compilation; 1,095 C# tests in each Debug/Release configuration; 5 parser and 18 release-policy cases; 18 isolated application smoke checks per portable flavor; 64 installer lifecycle assertions. Downloaded package payload/source hashes, test reports, native window safety checks and screenshots were reviewed. Tests use synthetic battery data and do not access HID or launch games.

Packages are unsigned. Physical battery behavior, normal live monitoring, real-game/exclusive fullscreen compatibility, actual cross-process click routing, physical mixed-DPI/monitor events and extended endurance remain unverified. No currently admitted Razer, Logitech or Alienware device supplies enough capacity telemetry for a physical battery-health result. Runtime estimates do not change that limitation.
